LESSON: POVERTY REDUCTION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.3: Poverty Reduction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Poverty Reduction. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the measures taken by African governments to reduce poverty?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the causes of poverty in Africa
2. apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: POVERTY REDUCTION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Poverty Reduction helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: POVERTY REDUCTION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain the causes of poverty in Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the causes of poverty in Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the causes of poverty in Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Poverty Reduction” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the causes of poverty in Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society

What this means
In this part you learn to apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Poverty Reduction.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Poverty Reduction is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Poverty Reduction” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain the causes of poverty in Africa)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Poverty Reduction. (skill: apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Poverty Reduction to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the causes of poverty in Africa.
3. Practise this skill: apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Poverty Reduction from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Poverty Reduction: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Poverty Reduction?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the measures taken by African governments to reduce poverty?
2. How does prudent utilisation of resources help to reduce poverty in society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Poverty Reduction means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the causes of poverty in Africa.
5. Be able to: apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
